transcript.text: Hi, our integrated fridge freezer (behind a kitchen door) - the fridge is around 10 degrees but the freezer seems ok. We had a power cut a week ago, not sure if related. Rented flat, can't really take it out.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. A fridge at around 10°C is too warm for safe chilled-food storage. As the freezer still seems OK, the more likely issue is cold air not getting from the freezer section into the fridge — often because vents are blocked or ice has built up behind a freezer panel. The power cut could also have left a setting or holiday/eco mode changed. You should report this to the landlord/letting agent now, particularly as it is an integrated appliance and you cannot reasonably pull it out. Move high-risk chilled food (meat, fish, dairy, cooked leftovers) to another working fridge if possible; do not rely on 10°C storage. 1. Check the temperature control/display. Set the fridge to about 3–5°C and freezer to -18°C, and make sure holiday/eco/demo mode is not selected. A wrong mode or warmer setting may be the whole cause. 2. Inside the fridge, make sure food is not pressed against vents on the back/top wall and that shelves are not packed tightly. If air cannot circulate, the fridge can stay warm even while the freezer is cold. 3. Look at the rear wall inside the freezer for a thick, snowy or solid sheet of ice. That points to an airflow/defrost problem and is normally a landlord/engineer repair rather than something to dismantle yourself. 4. Check both doors close flat, with no food or shelf fouling them, and that the rubber seals are not split, loose or badly folded. If the settings are normal, vents are clear, and it remains about 10°C after the doors have been kept shut as much as possible for 24 hours, it needs a repair visit. Do not pull an integrated unit out or remove panels yourself.
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

Thanks. The dial inside is on 3 of 5 and the fridge thermometer says 10C, freezer -16C. There's some frost on the freezer back wall but not loads. Doors both close ok. No burning smell or tripping. Should I turn the dial up?

Yes — turn it up one step, to 4. On this type of numbered dial, a higher number normally means colder. Avoid moving it repeatedly; give it 12–24 hours with the doors kept shut as much as possible. The freezer at -16°C is also a little warmer than the usual -18°C target, so this may be more than just the fridge setting. If the fridge is still near 10°C after the adjustment, or the freezer cannot reach about -18°C, report it as a cooling fault to the landlord/agent for an engineer. Likely areas are the cold-air circulation system (fan/damper) or cooling/control system; these are not sensible repairs to attempt by pulling out an integrated appliance.

candidates: Restricted cold-air flow or ice build-up between freezer and fridge (high)
Temperature setting or holiday/eco mode changed after the power cut (medium)
Door seal, blocked internal vents or over-packing (medium)

tags.checkGiven: Check the temperature dial or display: the fridge should be about 3–5°C and the freezer -18°C, and make sure no holiday / eco mode is on. Wa

plan: The fault they reported is: "fridge is around 10 degrees while freezer seems okay". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Cooling/control issue following the power cut or a setting that is too warm (medium)
